The 2002 FIFA World Cup (Korean: 2002 FIFA 월드컵 한국/일본, Japanese: 2002 FIFAワールドカップ 韓国/日本) also branded as Korea Japan 2002, was the 17th FIFA World Cup, the quadrennial football world championship for men's national teams organized by FIFA. It was held from 31 May to 30 June 2002 at sites in South Korea and Japan, with its final match hosted by Japan at International Stadium in Yokohama.

A field of 32 teams qualified for this World Cup, which was the first to be held in Asia, the first to be held outside of the Americas or Europe, as well as the first to be jointly hosted by more than one nation. Four teams (China, Ecuador, Senegal, and Slovenia) made their World Cup debuts, with Senegal being the only debutant to advance from the Group Stages and make it to the quarter-finals.

The tournament had several upsets and surprise results, which included the defending champions France being eliminated in the group stage after earning a single point without scoring a goal, and second favourites Argentina also being eliminated in the group stage. South Korea managed to reach the semi-finals, beating Poland, Portugal, Italy and Spain en route. They became the first team from outside of the UEFA, CONMEBOL, and CONCACAF regions to reach the semi-finals of the World Cup. Along with South Korea, Turkey made its first appearance in the semi-finals as well. However, the most potent team at the tournament, Brazil, prevailed, winning the final against Germany 2–0, making them the only country to have won the World Cup five times.[1] In the match for third place against South Korea, Turkey won 3–2, taking third place in only their second ever FIFA World Cup, and scored the fastest goal in the FIFA World Cup history (10.8 seconds after kick-off).[2]

The 2002 World Cup was the last one to use the golden goal rule and the last one to use the same ball for all matches. Starting in 2006 and continuing to the present, a ball with the same technical specifications but different colors has been used in the final. It was also the last World Cup in which the defending champions automatically qualified.

Host selectionedit
Main article: FIFA World Cup hosts
Korean Air Boeing 747 adorned with 2002 World Cup livery marking South Korea as co-hosts
Japanese 10,000 yen coin for the 2002 FIFA World Cup

South Korea and Japan were selected as hosts by FIFA on 31 May 1996.

Initially, South Korea, Japan and Mexico presented three rival bids. South Korea's entry into the race was seen by some as a response to the bid of political and sporting rival Japan.[3] FIFA leaders were split on whom to favor as host as politics within the world governing body held sway.[4] With Mexico regarded as a long shot, the battle to host the tournament came down to South Korea and Japan. The two Asian rivals went on a massive and expensive PR blitz around the world, prompting Sultan Ahmad Shah, the head of the Asian Football Confederation, to step in.[3] FIFA boss João Havelange had long backed the Japanese bid,[4] but his rival in FIFA, UEFA chief Lennart Johansson, sought to undermine Havelange's plans.[4] UEFA and the AFC viewed co-hosting between the two Asian rivals as the best option.[4] South Korea and Japan were finally faced with a choice of having no World Cup or a shared World Cup and they reluctantly chose to go along with co-hosting.[4] South Korea and Japan were chosen unanimously as co-hosts in preference to Mexico.[5]

This was the first World Cup to be hosted by more than one country, the second being the 2026 World Cup hosted by the United States, Mexico, and Canada. This is also the first ever World Cup to be hosted in Asia, the other being the 2022 World Cup hosted by Qatar twenty years later and the first World Cup to be held outside of Europe and the Americas.

The general secretary of South Korea's bidding committee, Song Young-shik, stated that FIFA was interested in staging some matches in North Korea in order to aid Korean reunification, but it was ruled out.[6] Though co-hosting the World Cup allowed Japan and South Korea to collaborate, the event did not significantly alter relations between the two countries, which have historically been strained.[7] Even so, the World Cup promoted a global vision of cooperation between Japan and South Korea.[7]

After being prevented from hosting along with South Korea, North Korea decided to host their own sports event, the Arirang Mass Games, at the same time as the World Cup. This is not unlike their course of action during the 1988 Seoul Olympics, where they decided to host the 13th World Festival of Youth and Students simultaneously.[8]

At the time the decision was made, Japan had never qualified for a World Cup tournament (although the Japanese did subsequently qualify for the 1998 competition). The only other countries to have been awarded a World Cup without previously having competed in a final tournament are Italy in 1934 and Qatar in 2022 (Uruguay hosted the first World Cup in 1930 so there was no prior tournament; they were defending Olympic champions from 1928).

Qualificationedit
Main article: 2002 FIFA World Cup qualification

199 teams attempted to qualify for the 2002 World Cup. The qualification process began with the preliminary draw held in Tokyo on 7 December 1999. Defending champions France and co-hosts South Korea and Japan qualified automatically and did not have to play any qualification matches. This was the final World Cup in which the defending champions qualified automatically and played the opening match.[9]

14 places were contested by UEFA teams (Europe), five by CAF teams (Africa), four by CONMEBOL teams (South America), four by AFC teams (Asia) and three by CONCACAF teams (North and Central America and the Caribbean). The remaining two places were decided by playoffs between AFC and UEFA and between CONMEBOL and OFC (Oceania). Four nations qualified for the finals for the first time: China, Ecuador, Senegal, and Slovenia.

Turkey qualified for the first time since 1954, Poland and Portugal both qualified for the first time since 1986, and Costa Rica and Uruguay qualified for the first time since 1990. Sweden, Russia, and the Republic of Ireland also returned after missing the 1998 World Cup. South Korea became the first nation from outside Europe or the Americas to appear in five successive finals tournaments.

All seven previous World Cup-winning nations (Argentina, Brazil, England, France, Germany, Italy, and Uruguay) qualified, which broke the record of most previous champions at a tournament before the record was broken again in 2014 with the addition of Spain (who won the 2010 tournament).

The highest-ranked team that did not qualify was the reigning Copa América champion Colombia (ranked 4th), while the lowest-ranked team that did qualify was China (ranked 50th).

Venuesedit

20 stadia were used for this tournament, the highest number for any FIFA World Cup at that point; South Korea and Japan each provided 10 stadiums, the vast majority of them newly built for the tournament. Groups A–D played all their matches in South Korea and Groups E–H played all their matches in Japan.[11] The stadiums in Daegu, Suwon, Yokohama, and Saitama all hosted 4 matches each, while the other 16 stadiums hosted 3 matches each. Notably, no matches were played in Tokyo, making it the second capital of a host country not to have a World Cup venue after Bonn of West Germany in 1974; however, the cities of Saitama and Yokohama which are part of the Greater Tokyo Area did host matches.[a]

Match officialsedit
show
List of match officials by confederation and country


There was much controversy over the refereeing in the tournament.[32] Decisions in the match between Italy and South Korea resulted in 400,000 complaints, and featured in ESPN's 10 most fabled World Cup controversies.[33] The match between Spain and South Korea featured two controversially disallowed Spanish goals, which Iván Helguera referred to as "a robbery" and led to Spanish press brandishing the officials "thieves of dreams", though FIFA dismissed the incident as human error.[34][35]

Squadsedit
Main article: 2002 FIFA World Cup squads

This was the first World Cup that featured squads of 23 players, an increase from 22 previously. Of the 23 players, three had to be goalkeepers.

Drawedit
Further information: 2002 FIFA World Cup seeding

The FIFA Organising Committee announced the eight seeded teams on 28 November 2001. The historic tradition to seed the hosts (South Korea and Japan) and holders (France) was upheld while the remaining five seeds were granted to the other five of the top six teams—ranked by their results in the last three FIFA World Cups (ratio 3:2:1) and their FIFA World Ranking position in the last month of the past three years (equal ratio).[36]

For the draw, the 32 teams were allocated into four pots; the eight top-seeded teams, were allocated in pot 1 and would be drawn/selected into the first position of the eight groups playing in the group stage. The remaining 24 unseeded teams, were allocated into three pots based on geographical sections, with the: 11 European teams in pot 2; two Asian teams and three South American teams in pot 3; three North American teams and five African teams in pot 4.[37]

The general principle was to draw one team from each pot into the eight groups, although with special combined procedures for pot 2 and pot 3, due to comprising more/less than eight teams – but sixteen teams in total. At the same time, the draw also needed to respect the geographical limitation, that each group cannot feature more than one team from each confederation, except for the European teams where the limitation was maximum two per group. Finally, special limitations were also stipulated to evenly distribute the presence of teams from each confederation between the groups playing respectively in Korea (group A-D) and Japan (group E-H); however, for political considerations, China could only be drawn for one of the groups playing in Korea.[37]

The draw took place at the Busan Exhibition and Convention Center in South Korea and was televised live on 1 December 2001.

The FIFA Organising Committee decided ahead of the draw to place the defending champions (France) in Group A while the co-hosts South Korea and Japan were placed in Group D and Group H respectively. The procedure for the draw comprised the following six steps:[37][38]

Pot 1 was used to draw, in alphabetical group order, the remaining five top-seeded teams for the first position of groups B, C, E, F and G; while respecting the restriction that one of the two South American seeds (Brazil and Argentina) had to play in a group played in South Korea (B/C) and the other had to play in a group played in Japan (E/F/G).
Pot 2 was used to draw one European team to each of the eight groups (drawing unrestricted in alphabetical order from A to H).
As per the FIFA rule of only allowing a maximum of two European teams in each group, the remaining three European teams from Pot 2 were subject to a second draw, to be put in either of the four groups containing a top-seeded South American team or Asian team. This was done by first drawing the European team from Pot 2, and then drawing which seeded opponent the European team should be paired with, from a special bowl with four blue balls containing the names of Brazil, Argentina, Japan and South Korea.
Pot 3 was used to draw one team to each of the five groups with an empty third slot (drawing in alphabetical order from A to H); while respecting the geographical restrictions, that:
None of the unseeded South American teams (Ecuador, Paraguay, Uruguay) from pot 3 could be drawn into a group with a seeded South American team (Brazil and Argentina).
None of the unseeded Asian teams (Saudi Arabia and China) from pot 3 could be drawn into a group with a seeded Asian team (South Korea and Japan in Group D and H); along with the overall rule that China had to play in South Korea (meaning either group A, B or C) and that Saudi Arabia had to play in Japan (meaning either group E, F or G).
Pot 4 was used to draw one team to each of the eight groups (drawing in alphabetical order from A to H); while respecting the restrictions that:
A minimum of one North American team and minimum of two African teams should be drawn to a group located in South Korea (Group A/B/C/D)
A minimum of one North American team and minimum of two African teams should be drawn to a group located in Japan (Group E/F/G/H)
To decide the match schedules, the exact group position number for the un-seeded teams in each group (2, 3 or 4), were also drawn immediately from eight special group bowls, after each respective team had been drawn from pot 2, 3 and 4.

Besides drawing the teams, the event also featured American vocalist Anastacia giving a debut public performance of the official song of the World Cup, "Boom".[39][40] The draw was conducted by FIFA general secretary Michel Zen-Ruffinen, and many celebrities helped with the draw such as former players Pelé, Johan Cruyff, Michel Platini, Enrique Borja, and Roger Milla, players of the time like Hong Myung-bo and Masami Ihara, women's football player Sun Wen, women's football referee Im Eun-ju, mountain climber Park Young-seok, actress Song Hye-kyo, and chess player Cho Hoon-hyun.

In each group, the teams played three matches, one against each of the other teams. Victories were granted 3 points, while a draw was equal to 1 point. After completion of the group stage, the best two teams of each group advanced to the Round of 16 in the knockout stage, in a way so all group winners started out meeting a runner-up from one of the other groups. This format was identical with the tournament structure being used in 1998. A total of 64 games were played, including the final and a match for third place between the two semi-final losers.

Group F was considered the group of death as it brought together Argentina, England, Nigeria, and Sweden.[39]

Round of 16edit
South Koreans watching their country's national team play Italy in the Round of 16 in Seoul Plaza

In the round of 16, Germany beat Paraguay 1–0 with a late goal by Oliver Neuville in Seogwipo. England defeated Denmark in Niigata 3–0, with all goals occurring in the first half of the game. Sweden and Senegal faced off in Ōita and finished 1–1 in regular time and it took a golden goal from Henri Camara in extra time to settle the game for Senegal 2–1, which led to Senegal becoming only the second African team to reach the last eight (after Cameroon in 1990). Spain and the Republic of Ireland played in Suwon, where Spain led most of the match 1–0 until a late penalty kick scored by Robbie Keane made the match go to extra time, where Spain emerged victorious in a penalty shoot-out. The United States beat CONCACAF rivals Mexico 2–0 in Jeonju with Brian McBride and Landon Donovan scoring the goals. Brazil defeated Belgium 2–0 in Kobe, with an amazing volley by Rivaldo and a splendid counter-attack goal by Ronaldo. Turkey ended co-hosts Japan's run with a 1–0 win in Miyagi, thanks to an Ümit Davala goal in the 12th minute. The other co-hosts, South Korea, defeated Italy 2–1 in extra time in Daejeon with a goal by Ahn Jung-hwan in the 117th minute.[42] South Korea's win ensured that, for the very first time in the Cup's history, teams from five continents – Europe, North America, South America, Africa and Asia – reached the quarter-finals of the same tournament.

Quarter-finalsedit

In the quarter-finals, England and Brazil squared off in Shizuoka, where Ronaldinho scored a free-kick goal over England's David Seaman early in the second half as Brazil won 2–1.[43] The United States lost to Germany 1–0 in Ulsan by a Michael Ballack goal in the 39th minute, but controversy surrounded the game when United States demanded the referee give a penalty for a goal-line handball by Torsten Frings in the 49th minute, but the referee did not award the penalty. South Korea got another success in Gwangju in a controversial manner, overcoming Spain 5–3 on penalties after a 0–0 draw in which the Spaniards twice thought they had scored while onside; however, the efforts were disallowed by the referee with controversial decisions.[44][34] The hosts became the first team in the Asian Football Confederation to reach the semi-finals of the World Cup, eclipsing the record of their North Korean counterparts who reached the quarter-finals in 1966. They also became the first World Cup semi-final team not from UEFA or CONMEBOL since the United States did it in the first World Cup in 1930. Turkey defeated Senegal 1–0 in Osaka, with a golden goal scored by İlhan Mansız in the 94th minute.

Finaledit
Main article: 2002 FIFA World Cup final

In the final match held in Yokohama, Japan, two goals from Ronaldo secured the World Cup for Brazil as they claimed victory over Germany.[49] Ronaldo scored twice in the second half and, after the game, won the Golden Shoe award for the tournament's leading scorer with eight goals.[50] This was the fifth time Brazil had won the World Cup, cementing their status as the most successful national team in the history of the competition. Brazil became the only team since Argentina in 1986 to win the trophy without needing to win a penalty shoot-out at some stage during the knockout phase and the total number of penalty shoot-outs (2) was the lowest since the four-round knockout format was introduced in 1986. Brazil also became the first team to win every match at a World Cup since 1970 and set a new record for highest aggregate goal difference (+14) for a World Cup winner. Brazil's captain Cafu, who became the first player to appear in three successive World Cup finals, accepted the trophy on behalf of the team.

Marketingedit
Sponsorshipedit
Coca-Cola was one of the sponsors of FIFA World Cup 2002.

The sponsors of the 2002 FIFA World Cup are divided into three categories: FIFA World Cup Sponsors and South Korea and Japan Suppliers.[55][56]

Ticket sales problemedit

The original domestic ticket allocation had fully sold out and the organising committee completed sales of tickets returned from the international allocation by the end of April. However, there were a significant number of empty seats at the opening matches.[72] It was gradually revealed that the World Cup Ticketing Bureau (WCTB) still had unsold tickets in its possession. After FIFA agreed to sell this inventory, JAWOC undertook sales over telephone and WCTB handled the internet sales.[73] For the second round Japan vs. Turkey match in Miyagi in particular, although it was reported by both parties that all tickets had been sold, some 700 seats remained empty.

Symbolsedit
Ato, Kaz and Nik were the 2002 World Cup mascots.
Mascotedit

The official mascots of the 2002 World Cup were Ato, Kaz and Nik (the Spheriks), orange, purple and blue (respectively) futuristic CGI creatures. Playing their own version of soccer called Atmoball, Ato is the coach while Kaz and Nik are players. The three individual names were selected from shortlists by users on the Internet and at McDonald's outlets in the host countries.[74]

Match balledit
Main article: Adidas Fevernova

The official match ball was the Fevernova, manufactured by Adidas.[75]

Musicedit

The official song was "Boom".[76] The official local song of this World Cup was "Let's Get Together Now". The official anthem was "Anthem".

Cultural eventedit
In Search of Fresh Air, banner by Ray L. Burggraf

The official FIFA cultural event of the 2002 World Cup was a flag festival called Poetry of the Winds.[77] Held in Nanjicheon Park, an area of the World Cup Park close to Seoul World Cup Stadium,[78][79] Poetry of the Winds was exhibited from 29 May to 25 June in order to wish success upon the World Cup and promote a festive atmosphere. During the flag art festival, hand-painted flags from global artists were displayed as a greeting to international guests in a manner that was designed to promote harmony.[77]

Concernsedit

The World Cup was originally going to be hosted either in Japan or in South Korea, but in the end both rivals had decided to share the hosting duties thus making this World Cup the first to have multiple host nations. However, there were concerns regarding the selection of hosts due to logistical issues caused by fans traveling across two separate sovereign nations as well as whether some of the 20 stadiums to be constructed for the World Cup would be ready in time for it or not. While political and infrastructural problems were eventually overcome, there still remained the issue of East Asia's wet season which could disrupt the play. The timing of the tournament thus had been altered to mitigate as much as possible against such issues, with the tournament kicking off on May 31 and due to run until June 30, the earliest date for a World Cup final since 1986.[80]

For European viewers, the time difference meant that matches were taking place in the local time morning, something viewers in Europe were not used to.[81][82] Some schools and businesses chose to open late on match days or set up communal watching events before the start of work.[83][84]

Economic impactedit

The tournament had a major economic impact on both South Korea and Japan, generating an estimated US$1.3 billion in revenue.[85] Spending from World Cup tourists in South Korea created US$307 million in direct income and US$713 million in valued added.[85] Japan spent an estimated US$5.6 billion on preparations for the event, which had a US$24.8 billion impact on the Japanese economy and accounted for 0.6% of their GDP in 2002.[86]

The **2008 FIFA Club World Cup final** was the final match of the [2008 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2008 FIFA Club World Cup"), an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament for the champion clubs from each of [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA")'s six continental confederations. The match took place at the International Stadium Yokohama, Japan, on 21 December 2008, and pitted [LDU Quito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LDU_Quito "LDU Quito") of Ecuador, the [CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONMEBOL "CONMEBOL") club champions, and [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") of England, the [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") club champions. Despite going down to ten men early in the second half, Manchester United won the match 1–0 thanks to a 73rd-minute goal from [Wayne Rooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Rooney "Wayne Rooney").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-2)

## Road to final

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Road to final")]

Both LDU Quito and Manchester United qualified for the competition at the semi-final stage, after winning their respective continental competition, the [2008 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Copa_Libertadores "2008 Copa Libertadores") and the [2007–08 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_UEFA_Champions_League "2007–08 UEFA Champions League").

LDU Quito's opening game was against [Mexican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federaci%C3%B3n_Mexicana_de_F%C3%BAtbol_Asociaci%C3%B3n "Federación Mexicana de Fútbol Asociación") side [Pachuca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.F._Pachuca "C.F. Pachuca"), who had defeated [Egyptian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_Football_Association "Egyptian Football Association") club [Al Ahly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ahly_SC "Al Ahly SC") 4–2 in the quarter-finals after [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_time "Extra time").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-3) Their semi-final match was played at the [National Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Stadium_(Tokyo) "Olympic Stadium (Tokyo)") in Tokyo on 17 December 2008.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-4) The Ecuadorian side scored two goals in the first 26 minutes through [Claudio Bieler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Bieler "Claudio Bieler") and [Luis Bolaños](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Bola%C3%B1os "Luis Bolaños"), securing their place in the Club World Cup final.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-5)

Manchester United's semi-final opponents were [Gamba Osaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamba_Osaka "Gamba Osaka"), who had previously defeated [Australian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_Federation_Australia "Football Federation Australia")[A-League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-League "A-League") premiers and [Asian Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_AFC_Champions_League "2008 AFC Champions League") runners-up [Adelaide United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide_United_FC "Adelaide United FC") (1–0) to move into the second semi-final on 18 December.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-6)[Nemanja Vidić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemanja_Vidi%C4%87 "Nemanja Vidić") and [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") opened the scoring in the first half, building up a two-goal lead at half-time. [Masato Yamazaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masato_Yamazaki_(footballer,_born_1981) "Masato Yamazaki (footballer, born 1981)") was the next to score in the 74th minute to bring Gamba back into contention, but [Wayne Rooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Rooney "Wayne Rooney") scored twice and [Darren Fletcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_Fletcher "Darren Fletcher") once within the next five minutes to extend United's lead. [Yasuhito Endō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasuhito_End%C5%8D "Yasuhito Endō") converted an 85th-minute [penalty kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") and [Hideo Hashimoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hideo_Hashimoto "Hideo Hashimoto") got a third for Gamba just minutes before the final whistle. The result was 5–3, taking Manchester United to the final.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-8)

The **2008 FIFA Club World Cup final** was the final match of the [2008 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2008 FIFA Club World Cup"), an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament for the champion clubs from each of [FIFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA "FIFA")'s six continental confederations. The match took place at the International Stadium Yokohama, Japan, on 21 December 2008, and pitted [LDU Quito](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/LDU_Quito "LDU Quito") of Ecuador, the [CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONMEBOL "CONMEBOL") club champions, and [Manchester United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manchester_United_F.C. "Manchester United F.C.") of England, the [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") club champions. Despite going down to ten men early in the second half, Manchester United won the match 1–0 thanks to a 73rd-minute goal from [Wayne Rooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Rooney "Wayne Rooney").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-2)

## Road to final

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Road to final")]

Both LDU Quito and Manchester United qualified for the competition at the semi-final stage, after winning their respective continental competition, the [2008 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Copa_Libertadores "2008 Copa Libertadores") and the [2007–08 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2007%E2%80%9308_UEFA_Champions_League "2007–08 UEFA Champions League").

LDU Quito's opening game was against [Mexican](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federaci%C3%B3n_Mexicana_de_F%C3%BAtbol_Asociaci%C3%B3n "Federación Mexicana de Fútbol Asociación") side [Pachuca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.F._Pachuca "C.F. Pachuca"), who had defeated [Egyptian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egyptian_Football_Association "Egyptian Football Association") club [Al Ahly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Ahly_SC "Al Ahly SC") 4–2 in the quarter-finals after [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extra_time "Extra time").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-3) Their semi-final match was played at the [National Stadium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olympic_Stadium_(Tokyo) "Olympic Stadium (Tokyo)") in Tokyo on 17 December 2008.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-4) The Ecuadorian side scored two goals in the first 26 minutes through [Claudio Bieler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claudio_Bieler "Claudio Bieler") and [Luis Bolaños](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Bola%C3%B1os "Luis Bolaños"), securing their place in the Club World Cup final.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-5)

Manchester United's semi-final opponents were [Gamba Osaka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamba_Osaka "Gamba Osaka"), who had previously defeated [Australian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Football_Federation_Australia "Football Federation Australia")[A-League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A-League "A-League") premiers and [Asian Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_AFC_Champions_League "2008 AFC Champions League") runners-up [Adelaide United](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adelaide_United_FC "Adelaide United FC") (1–0) to move into the second semi-final on 18 December.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-6)[Nemanja Vidić](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemanja_Vidi%C4%87 "Nemanja Vidić") and [Cristiano Ronaldo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cristiano_Ronaldo "Cristiano Ronaldo") opened the scoring in the first half, building up a two-goal lead at half-time. [Masato Yamazaki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Masato_Yamazaki_(footballer,_born_1981) "Masato Yamazaki (footballer, born 1981)") was the next to score in the 74th minute to bring Gamba back into contention, but [Wayne Rooney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wayne_Rooney "Wayne Rooney") scored twice and [Darren Fletcher](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Darren_Fletcher "Darren Fletcher") once within the next five minutes to extend United's lead. [Yasuhito Endō](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yasuhito_End%C5%8D "Yasuhito Endō") converted an 85th-minute [penalty kick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_kick_(association_football) "Penalty kick (association football)") and [Hideo Hashimoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hideo_Hashimoto "Hideo Hashimoto") got a third for Gamba just minutes before the final whistle. The result was 5–3, taking Manchester United to the final.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_FIFA_Club_World_Cup_final#cite_note-8)

The **2005 FIFA Club World Championship final** was an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") match played between [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC "São Paulo FC") of Brazil, the [CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONMEBOL "CONMEBOL") club champions, and [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") of England, the [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") club champions, on 18 December 2005 at the International Stadium Yokohama, Japan. It was the final match of the [2005 FIFA Club World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship "2005 FIFA Club World Championship"), a competition for the winners of the primary cup competitions of FIFA's continental members. The Club World Championship replaced the [Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_Cup_(1960%E2%80%932004) "Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)"), which both teams had competed in before. São Paulo had won the Intercontinental Cup twice in [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Intercontinental_Cup "1992 Intercontinental Cup") and [1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Intercontinental_Cup "1993 Intercontinental Cup"), while Liverpool had lost twice in [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Intercontinental_Cup "1981 Intercontinental Cup") and [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Intercontinental_Cup "1984 Intercontinental Cup").

The teams qualified for the championship by winning their continent's primary cup competition. São Paulo won the [2005 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Copa_Libertadores "2005 Copa Libertadores"), defeating Brazilian team [Atlético Paranaense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_Atl%C3%A9tico_Paranaense "Clube Atlético Paranaense")[5–1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Copa_Libertadores_Finals "2005 Copa Libertadores Finals"). Liverpool won the [2004–05 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Champions_League "2004–05 UEFA Champions League"), defeating Italian team [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Milan "A.C. Milan") 3–2 in a [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shootout_(association_football) "Penalty shootout (association football)") after the match had finished [3–3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2005 UEFA Champions League Final"). Both teams played one match in the championship en route to the final. São Paulo beat [2005 AFC Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_AFC_Champions_League "2005 AFC Champions League") winners [Al-Ittihad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ittihad_FC "Ittihad FC") 3–2, while Liverpool beat [2005 CONCACAF Champions' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_CONCACAF_Champions'_Cup "2005 CONCACAF Champions' Cup") winners [Deportivo Saprissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.D._Saprissa "C.D. Saprissa") 3–0.

Watched by a crowd of 66,821, São Paulo took the lead in the first half when [Mineiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineiro_(footballer,_born_1975) "Mineiro (footballer, born 1975)") scored. Liverpool missed a number of chances to equalise in the first half. In the second half they had the majority of the possession and also had three goals disallowed. Despite all their chances they were unable to score against São Paulo who held on to win the match 1–0.

## Route to the final

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Route to the final")]

[São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC "São Paulo FC") qualified for the [FIFA Club World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Club_World_Cup "FIFA Club World Cup") as the reigning [Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores "Copa Libertadores") winners. They had won the [2005 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Copa_Libertadores "2005 Copa Libertadores") beating [Atlético Paranaense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_Atl%C3%A9tico_Paranaense "Clube Atlético Paranaense")[5–1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Copa_Libertadores_Finals "2005 Copa Libertadores Finals") over two-legs in the final.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-2) It would be São Paulo's first appearance in the competition, although they had won the forerunner to the competition, the [Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_Cup_(1960%E2%80%932004) "Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)") twice, in [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Intercontinental_Cup "1992 Intercontinental Cup") and [1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Intercontinental_Cup "1993 Intercontinental Cup").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-rsssf-3)

[Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") had qualified for the Club World Championship as a result of winning the [2004–05 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Champions_League "2004–05 UEFA Champions League"). They beat Italian team [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Milan "A.C. Milan") 3–2 in a [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shootout_(association_football) "Penalty shootout (association football)") after the match had finished [3–3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2005 UEFA Champions League Final").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-4) Like São Paulo, Liverpool were competing in the competition for the first time, although they had appeared twice in the Intercontinental Cup, losing in [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Intercontinental_Cup "1981 Intercontinental Cup") and [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Intercontinental_Cup "1984 Intercontinental Cup").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-rsssf-3)

Both teams entered the competition in the semi-finals. São Paulo's opponents were the winners of the [2005 AFC Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_AFC_Champions_League "2005 AFC Champions League"), [Al-Ittihad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ittihad_FC "Ittihad FC"). A 3–2 victory with two goals from [Amoroso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1rcio_Amoroso "Márcio Amoroso") and a penalty from goalkeeper [Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni "Rogério Ceni") ensured São Paulo's progression to the final.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-5) Liverpool faced [2005 CONCACAF Champions' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_CONCACAF_Champions'_Cup "2005 CONCACAF Champions' Cup") winners [Deportivo Saprissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.D._Saprissa "C.D. Saprissa"). They won the match 3–0, [Peter Crouch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Crouch "Peter Crouch") scored twice and [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard") also scored as Liverpool reached the final.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-6)

## Match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Match")]

### Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Background")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Yokohamakokusai20041208.jpg/250px-Yokohamakokusai20041208.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yokohamakokusai20041208.jpg)

The International Stadium in Yokohama was the venue for the final

Both teams were well into their respective domestic competitions. São Paulo's domestic season had finished two weeks before the final. They finished the [2005 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Campeonato_Brasileiro_S%C3%A9rie_A "2005 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A") in 11th position after 42 games, they won and lost 16 games each and drew 10.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-7) Liverpool were in the middle of their domestic season, they were competing in the [2005–06 Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_FA_Premier_League "2005–06 FA Premier League"). They were second in the table and won their last match before the competition 2–0, against [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-fifa-8) The victory meant Liverpool had gone 10 matches without conceding a goal, which equalled a club record.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-9)

São Paulo manager [Paulo Autuori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulo_Autuori "Paulo Autuori") was adamant that his team would have to improve on their performance in the semi-final if they were to win the match: "We're going to have to improve certain aspects of our play if we want to win the final." Autuori was not worried about Liverpool's aerial threat, but was expecting them to keep the ball during the match: "English teams are well known for their aerial excellence, But Liverpool are a side that can keep the ball very well too as they proved when winning the Champions League."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-fifa-8)

Liverpool manager [Rafael Benítez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Ben%C3%ADtez "Rafael Benítez") would take control of the team for the final, despite the death of his father earlier in the week. Benitez was confident that his Liverpool team would be capable of beating São Paulo: "We are playing with confidence and strength. I think we can beat anyone." [Peter Crouch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Crouch "Peter Crouch"), who scored twice in the semi-finals, was as adamant as his manager about winning the competition. Adding that "We've not travelled all the way to Japan to go sightseeing."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-fifa-8)

### First half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: First half")]

[![Image 9: A man looking straight ahead with the top half of a suit visible](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni.jpg/250px-Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni.jpg)

[Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni "Rogério Ceni") captained São Paulo in the final.

Before the start of the match, a minute's silence was held in memory of Rafa Benítez's father Francisco, who died of heart failure on the Wednesday before the final. Both teams took the pitch wearing black armbands as a mark of respect.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-10) The match was delayed further when a fan of [Corinthians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_Club_Corinthians_Paulista "Sport Club Corinthians Paulista") invaded the pitch and gave São Paulo goalkeeper [Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni "Rogério Ceni") a [Bambi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bambi_(character) "Bambi (character)") toy, referencing the _Bambis_ nickname that city rivals associate São Paulo with.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-11) São Paulo lined up in a 3–5–2 formation, while Liverpool opted for a 4–4–1–1.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12) Liverpool had the first chance of the match inside the opening 79 seconds, when captain [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard")'s cross into the penalty area was met by [Fernando Morientes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Morientes "Fernando Morientes"), but the Spaniard headed wide. The Reds created more chances with [Luis García](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Garc%C3%ADa_(footballer,_born_1978) "Luis García (footballer, born 1978)") missing twice from headers.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-cnn-13) São Paulo had only created one chance, a shot from striker [Amoroso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1rcio_Amoroso "Márcio Amoroso"), but they began to grow in confidence. They pressed forward after Amoroso's shot and right-back [Cicinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicinho "Cicinho") nearly scored with a lob from the halfway line which just went over the crossbar.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-report-14)

São Paulo's pressure resulted in them taking the lead in the 27th minute, when a chipped pass from [Aloísio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alo%C3%ADsio_Chulapa "Aloísio Chulapa") found [Mineiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineiro_(footballer,_born_1975) "Mineiro (footballer, born 1975)"), who put the ball beyond Liverpool goalkeeper [Pepe Reina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_Reina "Pepe Reina") to give the Brazilians a 1–0 lead.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-bbc-15) It was the first goal Liverpool had conceded in over 1,041 minutes of play.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12) Immediately afterwards, from a corner, [Xabi Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xabi_Alonso "Xabi Alonso") almost assisted García if not for the woodwork.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-bbc-15) Liverpool had another chance 30 minutes into the match, but again he failed to score with a header.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-bbc-15) Gerrard had a chance to equalise five minutes later, but he put his shot wide after [Harry Kewell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Kewell "Harry Kewell") had passed him the ball.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-cnn-13) Liverpool continued to create chances and in the 39th minute, García saw his header into the far corner saved by Ceni.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-report-14) From the resulting corner, Liverpool defender [Sami Hyypiä](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sami_Hyypi%C3%A4 "Sami Hyypiä") shot straight at Ceni, who also saved a header from the Finn late in the first half.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-report-14)

### Second half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Second half")]

Liverpool had the first scoring opportunity of the half, six minutes into the second half. Liverpool were awarded a free kick 25 yards from the goal. Gerrard's subsequent shot was saved by Ceni.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-report-14) Ceni made another save soon afterwards when he tipped a cross from Kewell onto the crossbar.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-report-14) Liverpool did score on the hour mark, but the goal was disallowed. García's headed goal was ruled out for offside.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-bbc-15) Soon afterwards Morientes had another chance to score, but his overhead kick went over the crossbar.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-cnn-13) Liverpool had another goal disallowed soon afterwards. Alonso's corner from which Hyypiä was adjudged to have drifted out of play before the defender scored.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12)

São Paulo made the first substitution in the 75th minute when [Grafite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grafite "Grafite") replaced Aloísio. Liverpool made two substitutions four minutes later in an attempt to equalise. [John Arne Riise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Arne_Riise "John Arne Riise") and [Sinama Pongolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florent_Sinama_Pongolle "Florent Sinama Pongolle") replaced [Stephen Warnock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Warnock "Stephen Warnock") and [Mohamed Sissoko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohamed_Sissoko "Mohamed Sissoko"). They made their final substitution in the 85th minute when Peter Crouch replaced Morientes.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-stats-1) Liverpool had a third goal disallowed in the 89th minute; substitute Sinama Pongolle's goal was disallowed after the assistant referee had flagged García as being offside in the build-up to the goal.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12) Liverpool had a final chance before the end of the match, but García put his shot wide. No further goals were scored and the referee blew for full-time with the final score 1–0 to São Paulo.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-bbc-15)

## Post-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Post-match")]

[![Image 70](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/SPFC_squad_-_2005_-_01.jpg/250px-SPFC_squad_-_2005_-_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SPFC_squad_-_2005_-_01.jpg)

Tribute received by São Paulo from the Paulista Football Federation and President [Lula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_In%C3%A1cio_Lula_da_Silva "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva")_(far left)_ for winning the Cup.

Much of the talk after the match centred on Liverpool's three disallowed goals. [Rafael Benítez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Ben%C3%ADtez "Rafael Benítez") was incensed by the referee's decisions and remonstrated with the officials after the final whistle. Benítez was clear that at least one of those goals should not have been disallowed: "We knew that one of the goals was a goal, clear." He also questioned the competency of the officials stating: "You wouldn't get a Mexican referee and a Canadian linesman in the final of the World Cup."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12)[Luis García](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Garc%C3%ADa_(footballer,_born_1978) "Luis García (footballer, born 1978)"), who had a goal disallowed, summed up the feeling in the Liverpool dressing room: "We feel cheated."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12)

[Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni "Rogério Ceni") was named as man of the match and also won the Golden Ball as the best player of the competition. Ceni was gracious in receiving the awards stating: "The awards are nice to have but the win was not just about me" Ceni dedicated the awards to those at the club saying: "When I look in these awards I see the faces of my team-mates, the coach and everyone involved at the club." São Paulo manager was delighted with his team after the victory and agreed with Ceni that the victory was a team effort: "It was a collective victory" he also said that it was "a great achievement for the club." Goalscorer [Mineiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineiro_(footballer,_born_1975) "Mineiro (footballer, born 1975)") was equally overjoyed with the victory stating: "It is the happiest moment in my career."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-16)

The **2005 FIFA Club World Championship final** was an [association football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") match played between [São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC "São Paulo FC") of Brazil, the [CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONMEBOL "CONMEBOL") club champions, and [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") of England, the [UEFA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UEFA "UEFA") club champions, on 18 December 2005 at the International Stadium Yokohama, Japan. It was the final match of the [2005 FIFA Club World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship "2005 FIFA Club World Championship"), a competition for the winners of the primary cup competitions of FIFA's continental members. The Club World Championship replaced the [Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_Cup_(1960%E2%80%932004) "Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)"), which both teams had competed in before. São Paulo had won the Intercontinental Cup twice in [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Intercontinental_Cup "1992 Intercontinental Cup") and [1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Intercontinental_Cup "1993 Intercontinental Cup"), while Liverpool had lost twice in [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Intercontinental_Cup "1981 Intercontinental Cup") and [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Intercontinental_Cup "1984 Intercontinental Cup").

The teams qualified for the championship by winning their continent's primary cup competition. São Paulo won the [2005 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Copa_Libertadores "2005 Copa Libertadores"), defeating Brazilian team [Atlético Paranaense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_Atl%C3%A9tico_Paranaense "Clube Atlético Paranaense")[5–1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Copa_Libertadores_Finals "2005 Copa Libertadores Finals"). Liverpool won the [2004–05 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Champions_League "2004–05 UEFA Champions League"), defeating Italian team [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Milan "A.C. Milan") 3–2 in a [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shootout_(association_football) "Penalty shootout (association football)") after the match had finished [3–3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2005 UEFA Champions League Final"). Both teams played one match in the championship en route to the final. São Paulo beat [2005 AFC Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_AFC_Champions_League "2005 AFC Champions League") winners [Al-Ittihad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ittihad_FC "Ittihad FC") 3–2, while Liverpool beat [2005 CONCACAF Champions' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_CONCACAF_Champions'_Cup "2005 CONCACAF Champions' Cup") winners [Deportivo Saprissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.D._Saprissa "C.D. Saprissa") 3–0.

Watched by a crowd of 66,821, São Paulo took the lead in the first half when [Mineiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineiro_(footballer,_born_1975) "Mineiro (footballer, born 1975)") scored. Liverpool missed a number of chances to equalise in the first half. In the second half they had the majority of the possession and also had three goals disallowed. Despite all their chances they were unable to score against São Paulo who held on to win the match 1–0.

## Route to the final

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Route to the final")]

[São Paulo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Paulo_FC "São Paulo FC") qualified for the [FIFA Club World Championship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FIFA_Club_World_Cup "FIFA Club World Cup") as the reigning [Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores "Copa Libertadores") winners. They had won the [2005 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Copa_Libertadores "2005 Copa Libertadores") beating [Atlético Paranaense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_Atl%C3%A9tico_Paranaense "Clube Atlético Paranaense")[5–1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Copa_Libertadores_Finals "2005 Copa Libertadores Finals") over two-legs in the final.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-2) It would be São Paulo's first appearance in the competition, although they had won the forerunner to the competition, the [Intercontinental Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercontinental_Cup_(1960%E2%80%932004) "Intercontinental Cup (1960–2004)") twice, in [1992](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1992_Intercontinental_Cup "1992 Intercontinental Cup") and [1993](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1993_Intercontinental_Cup "1993 Intercontinental Cup").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-rsssf-3)

[Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C. "Liverpool F.C.") had qualified for the Club World Championship as a result of winning the [2004–05 UEFA Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004%E2%80%9305_UEFA_Champions_League "2004–05 UEFA Champions League"). They beat Italian team [Milan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A.C._Milan "A.C. Milan") 3–2 in a [penalty shootout](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shootout_(association_football) "Penalty shootout (association football)") after the match had finished [3–3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_UEFA_Champions_League_Final "2005 UEFA Champions League Final").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-4) Like São Paulo, Liverpool were competing in the competition for the first time, although they had appeared twice in the Intercontinental Cup, losing in [1981](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1981_Intercontinental_Cup "1981 Intercontinental Cup") and [1984](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1984_Intercontinental_Cup "1984 Intercontinental Cup").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-rsssf-3)

Both teams entered the competition in the semi-finals. São Paulo's opponents were the winners of the [2005 AFC Champions League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_AFC_Champions_League "2005 AFC Champions League"), [Al-Ittihad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ittihad_FC "Ittihad FC"). A 3–2 victory with two goals from [Amoroso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1rcio_Amoroso "Márcio Amoroso") and a penalty from goalkeeper [Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni "Rogério Ceni") ensured São Paulo's progression to the final.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-5) Liverpool faced [2005 CONCACAF Champions' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_CONCACAF_Champions'_Cup "2005 CONCACAF Champions' Cup") winners [Deportivo Saprissa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.D._Saprissa "C.D. Saprissa"). They won the match 3–0, [Peter Crouch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Crouch "Peter Crouch") scored twice and [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard") also scored as Liverpool reached the final.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-6)

## Match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Match")]

### Background

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: Background")]

[![Image 8](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/48/Yokohamakokusai20041208.jpg/250px-Yokohamakokusai20041208.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Yokohamakokusai20041208.jpg)

The International Stadium in Yokohama was the venue for the final

Both teams were well into their respective domestic competitions. São Paulo's domestic season had finished two weeks before the final. They finished the [2005 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_Campeonato_Brasileiro_S%C3%A9rie_A "2005 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A") in 11th position after 42 games, they won and lost 16 games each and drew 10.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-7) Liverpool were in the middle of their domestic season, they were competing in the [2005–06 Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005%E2%80%9306_FA_Premier_League "2005–06 FA Premier League"). They were second in the table and won their last match before the competition 2–0, against [Middlesbrough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middlesbrough_F.C. "Middlesbrough F.C.").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-fifa-8) The victory meant Liverpool had gone 10 matches without conceding a goal, which equalled a club record.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-9)

São Paulo manager [Paulo Autuori](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paulo_Autuori "Paulo Autuori") was adamant that his team would have to improve on their performance in the semi-final if they were to win the match: "We're going to have to improve certain aspects of our play if we want to win the final." Autuori was not worried about Liverpool's aerial threat, but was expecting them to keep the ball during the match: "English teams are well known for their aerial excellence, But Liverpool are a side that can keep the ball very well too as they proved when winning the Champions League."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-fifa-8)

Liverpool manager [Rafael Benítez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Ben%C3%ADtez "Rafael Benítez") would take control of the team for the final, despite the death of his father earlier in the week. Benitez was confident that his Liverpool team would be capable of beating São Paulo: "We are playing with confidence and strength. I think we can beat anyone." [Peter Crouch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Crouch "Peter Crouch"), who scored twice in the semi-finals, was as adamant as his manager about winning the competition. Adding that "We've not travelled all the way to Japan to go sightseeing."[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-fifa-8)

### First half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: First half")]

[![Image 9: A man looking straight ahead with the top half of a suit visible](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni.jpg/250px-Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni.jpg)

[Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni "Rogério Ceni") captained São Paulo in the final.

Before the start of the match, a minute's silence was held in memory of Rafa Benítez's father Francisco, who died of heart failure on the Wednesday before the final. Both teams took the pitch wearing black armbands as a mark of respect.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-10) The match was delayed further when a fan of [Corinthians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sport_Club_Corinthians_Paulista "Sport Club Corinthians Paulista") invaded the pitch and gave São Paulo goalkeeper [Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni "Rogério Ceni") a [Bambi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bambi_(character) "Bambi (character)") toy, referencing the _Bambis_ nickname that city rivals associate São Paulo with.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-11) São Paulo lined up in a 3–5–2 formation, while Liverpool opted for a 4–4–1–1.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12) Liverpool had the first chance of the match inside the opening 79 seconds, when captain [Steven Gerrard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_Gerrard "Steven Gerrard")'s cross into the penalty area was met by [Fernando Morientes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernando_Morientes "Fernando Morientes"), but the Spaniard headed wide. The Reds created more chances with [Luis García](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Garc%C3%ADa_(footballer,_born_1978) "Luis García (footballer, born 1978)") missing twice from headers.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-cnn-13) São Paulo had only created one chance, a shot from striker [Amoroso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/M%C3%A1rcio_Amoroso "Márcio Amoroso"), but they began to grow in confidence. They pressed forward after Amoroso's shot and right-back [Cicinho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cicinho "Cicinho") nearly scored with a lob from the halfway line which just went over the crossbar.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-report-14)

São Paulo's pressure resulted in them taking the lead in the 27th minute, when a chipped pass from [Aloísio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alo%C3%ADsio_Chulapa "Aloísio Chulapa") found [Mineiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineiro_(footballer,_born_1975) "Mineiro (footballer, born 1975)"), who put the ball beyond Liverpool goalkeeper [Pepe Reina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pepe_Reina "Pepe Reina") to give the Brazilians a 1–0 lead.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-bbc-15) It was the first goal Liverpool had conceded in over 1,041 minutes of play.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12) Immediately afterwards, from a corner, [Xabi Alonso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Xabi_Alonso "Xabi Alonso") almost assisted García if not for the woodwork.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-bbc-15) Liverpool had another chance 30 minutes into the match, but again he failed to score with a header.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-bbc-15) Gerrard had a chance to equalise five minutes later, but he put his shot wide after [Harry Kewell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harry_Kewell "Harry Kewell") had passed him the ball.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-cnn-13) Liverpool continued to create chances and in the 39th minute, García saw his header into the far corner saved by Ceni.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-report-14) From the resulting corner, Liverpool defender [Sami Hyypiä](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sami_Hyypi%C3%A4 "Sami Hyypiä") shot straight at Ceni, who also saved a header from the Finn late in the first half.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-report-14)

### Second half

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Second half")]

Liverpool had the first scoring opportunity of the half, six minutes into the second half. Liverpool were awarded a free kick 25 yards from the goal. Gerrard's subsequent shot was saved by Ceni.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-report-14) Ceni made another save soon afterwards when he tipped a cross from Kewell onto the crossbar.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-report-14) Liverpool did score on the hour mark, but the goal was disallowed. García's headed goal was ruled out for offside.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-bbc-15) Soon afterwards Morientes had another chance to score, but his overhead kick went over the crossbar.[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-cnn-13) Liverpool had another goal disallowed soon afterwards. Alonso's corner from which Hyypiä was adjudged to have drifted out of play before the defender scored.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12)

São Paulo made the first substitution in the 75th minute when [Grafite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grafite "Grafite") replaced Aloísio. Liverpool made two substitutions four minutes later in an attempt to equalise. [John Arne Riise](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Arne_Riise "John Arne Riise") and [Sinama Pongolle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Florent_Sinama_Pongolle "Florent Sinama Pongolle") replaced [Stephen Warnock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stephen_Warnock "Stephen Warnock") and [Mohamed Sissoko](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohamed_Sissoko "Mohamed Sissoko"). They made their final substitution in the 85th minute when Peter Crouch replaced Morientes.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-stats-1) Liverpool had a third goal disallowed in the 89th minute; substitute Sinama Pongolle's goal was disallowed after the assistant referee had flagged García as being offside in the build-up to the goal.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12) Liverpool had a final chance before the end of the match, but García put his shot wide. No further goals were scored and the referee blew for full-time with the final score 1–0 to São Paulo.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-bbc-15)

## Post-match

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Post-match")]

[![Image 70](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/SPFC_squad_-_2005_-_01.jpg/250px-SPFC_squad_-_2005_-_01.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:SPFC_squad_-_2005_-_01.jpg)

Tribute received by São Paulo from the Paulista Football Federation and President [Lula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luiz_In%C3%A1cio_Lula_da_Silva "Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva")_(far left)_ for winning the Cup.

Much of the talk after the match centred on Liverpool's three disallowed goals. [Rafael Benítez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rafael_Ben%C3%ADtez "Rafael Benítez") was incensed by the referee's decisions and remonstrated with the officials after the final whistle. Benítez was clear that at least one of those goals should not have been disallowed: "We knew that one of the goals was a goal, clear." He also questioned the competency of the officials stating: "You wouldn't get a Mexican referee and a Canadian linesman in the final of the World Cup."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12)[Luis García](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luis_Garc%C3%ADa_(footballer,_born_1978) "Luis García (footballer, born 1978)"), who had a goal disallowed, summed up the feeling in the Liverpool dressing room: "We feel cheated."[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-guardian-12)

[Rogério Ceni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rog%C3%A9rio_Ceni "Rogério Ceni") was named as man of the match and also won the Golden Ball as the best player of the competition. Ceni was gracious in receiving the awards stating: "The awards are nice to have but the win was not just about me" Ceni dedicated the awards to those at the club saying: "When I look in these awards I see the faces of my team-mates, the coach and everyone involved at the club." São Paulo manager was delighted with his team after the victory and agreed with Ceni that the victory was a team effort: "It was a collective victory" he also said that it was "a great achievement for the club." Goalscorer [Mineiro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mineiro_(footballer,_born_1975) "Mineiro (footballer, born 1975)") was equally overjoyed with the victory stating: "It is the happiest moment in my career."[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2005_FIFA_Club_World_Championship_final#cite_note-16)
